meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was a zero entered on Owen's essay before anyone called me?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. People draft elsewhere and paste it in. You still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before that zero went in.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Pull it up. And "what the history shows" doesn't answer whether he could have pasted it from somewhere else.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misquote. A misremembered line isn't a procedure. Put the text in front of me, and the history, and I'll search it myself.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Arguments change between an outline and an essay; that's what drafting is. Hand me both documents, with the dates on them. And then answer my question: did anyone speak to Owen before the zero?
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
So that's your answer: you spoke to him on the second, without me. A seventeen-year-old put on the spot says "like, being stuck", and you call that evidence? Show me the note you wrote that day.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend at a desk; of course they differ. You keep telling me what you have. Put it in front of me.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because a machine's score isn't evidence, and the company that sells it says so. Keep it out of anything you write. Now turn the screen around.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4. In writing, with nothing on his record. And I still haven't seen one document.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Ten minutes. I'm not answering that until I've seen what the rewrite is for. Show me the history and the outline, then ask me again.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
The December first deadline is the point, yes. But I'm not picking a day for a rewrite until I've seen the history and the outline with my own eyes. Turn the screen.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
No. I've agreed to nothing, because I still haven't seen the history or the outline. Show me those, then ask again.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
Yes. The version history, the outline and your note from the second, in front of me. Now.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn and the version history, the outline and your note from November 2 put in front of me. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position and agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn and every document in her hands; the fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under 4.4, which you offered, but she would not take it before seeing evidence, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling home in one plain sentence, which earned a flat okay because it took away her sharpest procedural complaint.
What cost ground: You offered the rewrite and asked her to pick a day before any document was in front of her, so she heard a deal with nothing behind it.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your late-night editing times came close to that night, but they prove nothing about the essay, and they are part of why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When you first mention the version history, say that you are turning the screen and put the history and the outline in front of her at once, so the 4.4 offer lands on evidence she has already checked.
